candidates.label: Cardiac sarcoidosis with high-grade AV block, biventricular systolic dysfunction, and mediastinal lymphadenopathy
Giant cell myocarditis with complete heart block and biventricular failure
Cardiac amyloidosis (AL or ATTR) with conduction disease and heart failure
Lyme carditis with high-grade AV block (despite negative serology)
Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy with left ventricular involvement and conduction disease

response.rationale: The combination of mediastinal and bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy, non-ischemic mid-myocardial late gadolinium enhancement on cardiac MRI, biventricular dysfunction, and conduction abnormalities (LBBB, high-grade AV block) strongly favors cardiac sarcoidosis. Normal coronary arteries exclude ischemic cardiomyopathy. Negative Lyme serology reduces the likelihood of Lyme carditis. Other infiltrative or inflammatory cardiomyopathies are less likely given the prominent lymphadenopathy and specific MRI pattern.
